title: How iron rusts
caption: Under a drop of water, iron at the centre (where oxygen is scarce) is oxidised to Fe²⁺; electrons flow through the metal to the edge, where oxygen is reduced to OH⁻. Fe²⁺ and OH⁻ meet to form Fe(OH)₂, which oxidises further to rust, Fe₂O₃·xH₂O.
alt: A water droplet on iron: the anode region in the middle and the cathode region at the edge, with the two half-equations.
description: E°cell = 0.40 − (−0.44) = 0.84 V, so the reaction is feasible.
